About the Scholarship

Kent’s AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards support new doctoral researchers in eligible arts, humanities and related subjects. International recipients receive a waiver of the overseas tuition fee difference. University of Kent invites applications for a PhD position in this area: AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards at University of Kent 2027. Research areas covered include History. The role is based in Canterbury, United Kingdom. According to the listing, the opportunity is fully funded; financial support is listed as £21,805/year. Applications close 15 February 2027, 23:59 GMT.

Research Areas

  • Arts
  • humanities and related eligible subjects

Funding and Duration

ComponentDetails
FundingHome tuition plus full International fee-gap waiver; further research support by application.
MaintenanceGBP 21,805/year (published reference; confirm applicable award-year rate)
Duration3.5 years minimum; up to 4 with development activities

Eligibility and Requirements

First/2:1-equivalent degree or accepted equivalent qualifications/experience; new doctoral students. Overseas awards are capped at up to one-third. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
Recruitment2027 deadline advertised
Deadline15 February 2027, 23:59 GMT

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.kent.ac.uk/courses/postgraduate/apply

Source: kent.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 15 February 2027, 23:59 GMT - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Apply for a Kent PhD. Complete the AHRC form with supervisor support and email it with your name and KentVision applicant ID to dtpenquiries@kent.ac.uk.

Four awards per annual cohort across the eligible arts, humanities, law, politics, architecture and language areas.

About University of Kent

The University of Kent offers postgraduate research across arts, humanities, law, politics and other disciplines. Based in Canterbury, it supports doctoral applicants through academic schools and the Graduate and Researcher College, including competitive AHRC funding.

Official details: Programme information

Application route: Application form or official instructions

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
